Block

Concept 3 of 4 · Direction: Bold modern retail

This concept treats Evolution as a confident modern retailer that happens to sell golf. Strong colour blocks (cobalt, coral, lilac; deliberately not green) divide the homepage into clear, tappable zones, and a single chunky grotesk carries everything. The hero is a bento of three blocks that each answer one of the five-second questions: Motocaddy, free fitting, membership. Directly underneath, a three-question trolley finder (GPS? hilly? 18 or 36 holes?) gets a buyer to a short list in three taps. Products are big cut-outs on flat colour with prices you can read from across the room. It is the most conversion-focused of the four.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

The hero and the three pillar tiles merge into one bento block (Motocaddy / free fitting / membership). A trolley finder is added straight after the hero, ahead of the range, because it is the fastest path to the right trolley. The trust row becomes a single Trustpilot score block lower down; guides shrink to a list because this concept prioritises shopping over reading.

Imagery and photography

Products do the talking: oversized cut-outs on flat colour, cropped big and allowed to bleed off the edge. Lifestyle photography is optional and, where used, bright and graphic (a trolley against a hedge or sky, shot square-on), never moody fairways.

Headline copy

H1: “Motocaddy. Sorted.”

Sub: “The UK specialist for Motocaddy electric trolleys and custom‑fitted clubs.”

Bento: “Fitting is free.” · “Members are £60.90 up on an M5.”

Finder: “Find your trolley in three taps”

Motion

Snappy and physical: blocks scale slightly on press, the finder count ticks up and down as answers change, quick-add confirms with a short colour flash. Nothing slow.

Trade-offs

Does wellFastest route to a trolley (finder plus shelf); the clearest prices; the most modern and least ‘golf shop’ look; needs almost no lifestyle photography, so it could launch soonest.
Weaker onLeast premium-feeling for the fitting service and the expertise story; a bold palette needs discipline from merchandisers to avoid looking like a sale. Colour away from green is a brand departure that needs owner buy-in.
Build effortMedium. The finder needs the trolley metafields (GPS, DHC, battery holes) to exist; the rest is a straightforward component set.
Photography neededLow: clean cut-outs (already available). Optional graphic lifestyle shots.
Suits bestMobile shoppers who already know they want a Motocaddy and want the right one quickly; younger golfers; gift buyers.

EG monogram: Bold ‘EG’ in Bricolage 800, ink on white or white on cobalt, inside a square block (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
